annotation.title_clean: EHAZOP: A Proof of Concept Ethical Hazard Analysis of an Assistive Robot
annotation.title_en: EHAZOP: A Proof of Concept Ethical Hazard Analysis of an Assistive Robot
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Menon, C.; Rainer, A.; Holthaus, P.; Lakatos, G.; Carta, S.
annotation.summary_en: Presents EHAZOP, an ethical hazard analysis method adapted from safety-engineering HAZOP using guide words and 'what-if' questions, and applies it in a proof-of-concept workshop on the Ari assistive robot in domestic settings. It identifies diverse ethical hazards, including novel ones such as erosion of confidence, robot addiction and dehumanisation.
key_provisions_or_claims: EHAZOP adapts HAZOP guide words (more, less, early, late, opposite, in addition, never) to ethical hazards.
Hazards are assessed relative to user expectations of robot functions and characteristics.
Low-overhead facilitated process enables input from diverse, non-technical stakeholders.
Proof of concept with the Ari robot identified hazards like loss of autonomy, robot addiction, dehumanisation and erosion of confidence.
Some identified hazards were not in existing ethical hazard enumerations, showing novelty.
